findings.highlight: why is he suddenly concerned about how Sakura’s doing?
findings.evidenceJa: なんだってここで桜の体調を知りたがるのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders why Kirei wants to know Sakura’s condition here.
findings.explanation: The English promotes the request for information into personal concern before Kirei explains his purpose.

findings.highlight: What’s going on?
findings.evidenceJa: どんな風の吹き回しだよ
findings.governingReading: Shirou suspiciously asks what strange wind or change of heart has brought this on.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the pointed idiom to a generic request for explanation.

findings.highlight: Your body is in critical condition
findings.evidenceJa: おまえも危うい体だが
findings.governingReading: Kirei calls Shirou’s body precarious or endangered.
findings.explanation: “Critical condition” turns the warning into a clinical diagnosis.

findings.highlight: fighting is like committing suicide for you
findings.evidenceJa: 戦いそのものが自殺行為に等しい愚行だ
findings.governingReading: For Shirou now, fighting itself is a folly equivalent to suicidal conduct.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the suicide comparison but drops Kirei’s condemnation of the act as folly.

findings.highlight: is that woman truly so valuable to you
findings.evidenceJa: あの娘は衛宮士郎にとって
findings.governingReading: Kirei refers to Sakura as “that girl” while questioning her value to Shirou.
findings.explanation: “That woman” alters Kirei’s coldly distanced form of reference.

findings.highlight: To save a life is to satisfy one’s desire.
findings.evidenceJa: 生かすという事は欲望を満たすという事
findings.governingReading: Kirei says that keeping someone alive means satisfying desire.
findings.explanation: “Save a life” reframes continued preservation as a discrete rescue and makes the aphorism more conventionally altruistic.

findings.highlight: his usual criticism
findings.evidenceJa: いつもの皮肉
findings.governingReading: Shirou calls Kirei’s remarks his usual irony or sarcasm.
findings.explanation: The English replaces Kirei’s characteristic ironic provocation with generic criticism.

findings.highlight: I’ll forgive you for what you did yesterday
findings.evidenceJa: 昨日の事は水に流してあげる
findings.governingReading: Rin imperiously offers to let yesterday’s events wash away.
findings.explanation: The English assigns a specific wrongdoing to Shirou and makes Rin grant him personal forgiveness.

findings.highlight: Her manner is pompous
findings.evidenceJa: 偉そうに胸を張りつつ
findings.governingReading: Rin physically puffs out her chest importantly while making her pronouncement.
findings.explanation: The English replaces visible comic posture with an abstract personality judgment.

findings.highlight: I’m saying we can cooperate!
findings.evidenceJa: 協力してあげてもいいって言ってるのっ
findings.governingReading: Rin says she may deign to cooperate for Shirou’s benefit.
findings.explanation: The English removes the permissive, face-saving posture that carries Rin’s voice.

findings.highlight: I can cooperate with you!
findings.evidenceJa: それまで手を組んであげてもいい
findings.governingReading: Rin offers to join forces until their shared goal of defeating Zouken is achieved.
findings.explanation: The English omits the endpoint and makes the renewed alliance sound indefinite.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka continues angrily.
findings.evidenceJa: 文句ありげな視線でまくし立てる
findings.governingReading: Rin rattles on under a complaining look.
findings.explanation: The English replaces her performative complaint and rapid delivery with anger.

findings.highlight: a great fortune
findings.evidenceJa: これ以上ない程の幸運だった
findings.governingReading: To Shirou, the sudden offer is the greatest possible stroke of luck.
findings.explanation: The English weakens the superlative relief and uses the unnatural count phrase “a great fortune.”

findings.highlight: I know I’m being too happy
findings.evidenceJa: 自分でもはしゃいでるって分かっている
findings.governingReading: Shirou knows he is getting carried away or acting giddy.
findings.explanation: The English turns outwardly excited conduct into an excessive quantity of happiness.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka retreats quickly.
findings.evidenceJa: だだ、と慌てて後退する遠坂
findings.governingReading: Rin hurriedly scuttles backward from the vigorous handshake.
findings.explanation: The English deletes her panic and the comic manner of retreat.

findings.highlight: she looks at my left arm
findings.evidenceJa: 左腕をじろじろと見る
findings.governingReading: Rin stares over Shirou’s left arm with conspicuous scrutiny.
findings.explanation: The English removes the sustained, socially noticeable inspection.

findings.highlight: since it’s a matter of course
findings.evidenceJa: そりゃ当然、と頷く
findings.governingReading: Shirou nods because of course he knows whose arm it is.
findings.explanation: The literal phrase is stiff, Japanese-shaped English in otherwise internal narration.

findings.highlight: makes a ridiculous demand
findings.evidenceJa: とんでもないコトを言い切った
findings.governingReading: Rin flatly declares an outrageous proposition.
findings.explanation: The English changes the speech act from an asserted ownership claim into a demand.

findings.highlight: I try to figure out what Tohsaka means.
findings.evidenceJa: トンチを働かせる
findings.governingReading: Shirou sets his riddle-solving wit to work on Rin’s baffling claim.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the goal but removes the comic description of his mental method.

findings.highlight: claim his ownership
findings.evidenceJa: 所有権を言い出す
findings.governingReading: Illya objects to Rin beginning to assert ownership rights over Shirou.
findings.explanation: “His ownership” grammatically names ownership possessed by Shirou rather than ownership of him.

findings.highlight: Illya can be reasonable, after all.
findings.evidenceJa: イリヤは時にまっとうなコトを言ってくれる
findings.governingReading: Shirou observes that Illya says sensible things at times.
findings.explanation: “After all” implies an established conclusion and loses the joke’s sharply limited “sometimes.”

findings.highlight: there’s no way he can be yours
findings.evidenceJa: リンにあげられるワケない
findings.governingReading: Illya says that because Shirou is hers, she cannot give him to Rin.
findings.explanation: The English omits Illya’s asserted ownership and transfer action, weakening the ownership-rights joke.

findings.highlight: I almost went berserk myself.
findings.evidenceJa: 暴れる寸前だった
findings.governingReading: Rin says she was on the verge of lashing out or going on a rampage at school.
findings.explanation: The English uses “berserk,” importing the nearby Servant name/class resonance absent from her wording.

findings.highlight: I can choose to keep him alive or not
findings.evidenceJa: 生かすのも殺すのもわたし
findings.governingReading: Illya claims authority both to let Shirou live and to kill him.
findings.explanation: “Or not” euphemizes the explicit killing half of her casually cruel ownership claim.

findings.highlight: I can almost hear their teeth grinding as they glower
findings.evidenceJa: 軋み音が聞こえそうなほど睨み合う二人
findings.governingReading: The women glare so intensely that Shirou imagines a structural creaking sound.
findings.explanation: The English invents grinding teeth and relocates the comic sound image into their mouths.

findings.highlight: I wait for it to end.
findings.evidenceJa: 眉間に皺を寄せながら、黙って決着がつくのを待つ
findings.governingReading: Shirou silently waits for a decision with his brow furrowed.
findings.explanation: The English deletes his visible strain and weakens a contest being decided into something merely ending.

findings.highlight: fighting solves nothing
findings.evidenceJa: 言い合いでは決着がつかない
findings.governingReading: The two judge that their verbal argument will not settle the issue.
findings.explanation: The English broadens the comic quarrel into fighting in general.

findings.highlight: you don’t want her
findings.evidenceJa: シロウがイヤがってる
findings.governingReading: Illya says Rin has failed to notice that Shirou dislikes the proposed arrangement.
findings.explanation: The English makes Shirou reject Rin personally rather than object to being claimed as her Servant.

findings.highlight: You’re mine, right?
findings.evidenceJa: わたしのものでいいんだよね？
findings.governingReading: Illya coaxingly asks whether Shirou is fine with being hers.
findings.explanation: The English removes the permission-shaped “is it okay” and hardens the preferred answer into direct possession.
